meta.note: Lines are schematic. They follow the general direction of each corridor as described in official documents and do not show actual infrastructure alignments.

corridors.name: New Eurasian Land Bridge
corridors.description: A rail-based corridor from China's east coast through Kazakhstan, Russia and Belarus to Western Europe, carrying much of the China–Europe freight train traffic.

corridors.name: China–Mongolia–Russia Economic Corridor
corridors.description: Links northern China with Mongolia and Russia through two main routes, via Erenhot–Ulaanbaatar and via Manzhouli. Agreed in 2016.

corridors.name: China–Central Asia–West Asia Economic Corridor
corridors.description: Runs from Xinjiang through Central Asia to Iran and on to Türkiye and the Mediterranean.

corridors.name: China–Indochina Peninsula Economic Corridor
corridors.description: Connects southern China (Kunming, Nanning) with mainland Southeast Asia down to Singapore.

corridors.name: China–Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC)
corridors.description: A bilateral corridor launched in 2013 that links Kashgar in Xinjiang with the Arabian Sea ports of Gwadar and Karachi, and that covers energy, transport and special economic zones.

corridors.name: Bangladesh–China–India–Myanmar Corridor / China–Myanmar Economic Corridor
corridors.description: The original four-country BCIM corridor has seen limited progress, and India has not endorsed the BRI. Since 2017–2018, China and Myanmar have pursued a bilateral China–Myanmar Economic Corridor towards Mandalay, Yangon and Kyaukphyu.
